arguments.hypothesis: On the frozen task, robot, evaluator and fixed controller controller.gvs_nmpc@7.0.0, raising the recipe tip-speed cost weights — control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight above the already-tested 0.05 and/or control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight above the already-tested 0.0 — will lower the sampled final-window holding max world tip speed (tested candidate 1.1750052670100422 m/s, F1728, F1310) relative to that tested candidate while terminal reach stays inside the 0.01 m tolerance and the recorded force bound violation stays 0 N. The claim is scoped to exactly the changed configurations this bounded coordinate batch executes on the shared frozen baseline; it is a local candidate-comparison statement, not a closed-loop causal attribution and not a statement about the whole weight range.
arguments.rationale: Linked to the accepted single-context diagnosis and the performed plans check; this is the current authorized development pilot plan and executes no batch and promotes no candidate. Observation (performed-check aliases): the tested candidate fails the sampled final holding window while passing terminal reach — holding max error 0.05650455971948983 m (F1730) vs position limit 0.01 m (F1712), holding max speed 1.1750052670100422 m/s (F1728) vs speed limit 0.02 m/s (F1745), terminal error 0.00869890424761182 m (F1734) inside tolerance with terminal_reach_passed true (F1694), joint_reach_holding_passed false (F1541); the sealed comparison remains physical_tradeoff (F1324) with holding improvements (F1465, F1596) offset by terminal-error and computation worsening (F1546, F1433, baseline terminal error F1558); the performed plans view recorded User_Requested_Stop termination (F160) with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible (F167) and accepted plans (F177), 6 noninitialization selections over 35 updates (F153, F154), sampled applied tensions up to 7.999987676698501 N at update 32 (F157) with 0 N recorded violation (F1534) on a finite valid execution (F1442). Hypothesis (scope-qualified, explicitly not causal): raising the two tip-speed weights lowers the sampled hold speed relative to the tested candidate without breaking terminal reach or the force bound; it covers only the configurations actually executed, and no dominant-cause or whole-range claim is made. Proposed test: a coordinate batch on exactly the two granted paths with fresh executions and the frozen comparison. The prior step 0.0 -> 0.05 moved the sampled hold speed only 1.5810152739742807 -> 1.1750052670100422 m/s (F1474, F1728), so promise is uncertain. Recommendation/candidate separation: retained diagnostic positions (no closed-loop causal attribution; further weight-only tuning is low-yield on this baseline) are kept as diagnostic views and are independent of selecting the controller candidate; nothing is selected or promoted here. Fixed: robot, task, acceptance, controller_implementation and other_numerical_settings unchanged, fixed_controller controller.gvs_nmpc@7.0.0, method search.family_coordinate@1.0.0. Variables are only control/recipe/holding_tip_speed_weight and control/recipe/terminal_tip_speed_weight with granted bounds [0,1]; saved starting values 0.05 and 0.0 lie in-domain, both domains have nonzero width and include the saved values, and the 0.25 coordinate step stays clear of the forbidden (0, 0.0001) interval (0.05+0.25=0.30, 0.0+0.25=0.25). The proposal list includes the saved start point and duplicates; duplicates are not new backend attempts. Costs restated for the rejected-draft repair: max_backend_attempts=3 with planned backend_solves=3, tool_calls=24 (>=4 per new execution), wall_s=2970 (>=990 per new execution), model_calls=4, worker_calls=0; no separate numerical screening and no new baseline. Stop after two distinct changed configurations complete simulation/evaluation/profile even if joint acceptance occurs earlier, and protect ~600 s and four provider/tool slots for interpretation and delivery. Termination is kept distinct from convergence, applied updates distinct from optimized selections, wall deadlines distinct from simulated steps, and terminal reach distinct from holding. A validated plan still requires a future grant.
stopping_conditions: Stop normally after TWO distinct changed configurations have completed simulation.run, evaluation.run and control.profile_report, even if joint_reach_holding_acceptance is reached earlier.
Stop after at most 6 candidate proposals and at most 3 new full backend attempts; stop immediately on a material failure under stop_on_material_failure.
Stop with no promotion and no selection of any controller candidate; report every unexecuted candidate as not_run and keep ~600 s plus four provider/tool slots for interpretation and delivery.
Report raw termination status and controller policy stop reason separately, and report zero bound violation separately from legal near-bound input.
weakening_observations: A prior paired change (holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0 -> 0.05) reduced the sampled final-window hold max speed only from 1.5810152739742807 m/s (F1474) to 1.1750052670100422 m/s (F1728, F1310), still far above the 0.02 m/s limit (F1745); weight-only leverage on this term was small at that step, so the expected yield of further weight increases is weak to uncertain.

The same change worsened other physical and cost metrics: terminal error delta +0.001056295661744434 m (F1546) against candidate terminal error 0.00869890424761182 m (F1734), mean complete-update delta +0.5154540428891785 s (F1433) against candidate mean 17.77877309145406 s (F1743), holding error delta -0.001633544566242727 m (F1465), holding speed delta -0.4060100069642385 m/s (F1596); the sealed comparison is classified physical_tradeoff (F1324), so a further increase may again trade one physical metric for another.

Controller-side plan records from the performed check show termination by User_Requested_Stop (F160) with policy_stop_reason budget_best_feasible (F167) and accepted plans (F177), so the accepted plan at sampled updates may be compute-budget limited rather than weight limited; a weight-only batch cannot separate these explanations.

Sampled applied tensions reached 7.999987676698501 N at update 32 (F157) near the 8.0 N per-tendon limit while the recorded bound violation is 0 N (F1534); raising speed penalties could push loading closer to that bound, and zero violation does not exclude legal near-bound input.

Holding coverage is only the final 0.05 s (6 samples) with no continuous-time guarantee, joint_reach_holding_passed is false (F1541), and no closed-loop counterfactual replay or causal-attribution tool exists; a small batch describes only the candidates actually tested.
